plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (MgF2/HfO2 chirped stack) per feedback directives. Four complementary routes: (1) geometric chirp with r∈[1.08,1.12] and 85nm HfO2 cap per directive, (2) SiO2/HfO2 material alternative from evidence-supported UV filter pairs, (3) reduced 16-layer count to test layer-efficiency tradeoff, (4) AR-matched periodic photonic crystal structure from CorpusId:199509322 evidence. All routes preserve parent_route_id='route_02', maintain 255-280nm passband with 300-1100nm rejection objectives, and use only allowed evidence IDs.

routes.title: Geometric chirp MgF2/HfO2 stack with thickness ratio template and HfO2 cap
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A geometric progression thickness template (ratio r∈[1.08,1.12]) with 85nm HfO2 upper bound will produce candidates with higher UV transmission by pre-filtering absorption-dominated thick-HfO2 configurations, enabling the optimizer to focus computational budget on stopband engineering within feasible transmission windows.
routes.design_principle: Replace free-parameter initialization with geometric progression template for both high- and low-index layers to enforce physically realistic chirp gradient. HfO2 thickness cap prevents deep-UV absorption losses while maintaining visible/NIR rejection capability.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: air | [MgF2 | HfO2]_10 | fused_silica substrate. Exact layer count: 20 finite layers.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with geometric progression initialization r∈[1.08,1.12]
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 thickness capped at 85nm for UV transparency
geometric chirp reproducible via calibrated deposition rate
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
Geometric progression chirp for broadband stopband expansion
expected_advantages: Systematic chirp gradient improves visible/NIR rejection bandwidth
Initialization template guides optimizer toward physically feasible region
known_risks: Geometric constraint may limit optimal thickness combinations
85nm HfO2 cap may reduce stopband depth if insufficient optical thickness
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer alternating MgF2/HfO2 planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate for normal incidence. Initialize layer thicknesses using geometric progression with ratio r sampled uniformly from [1.08, 1.12] for both MgF2 and HfO2 layers. Enforce hard upper bound of 85nm on all HfO2 layer thicknesses during initialization and optimization. MgF2 layers may range 20-200nm. Evaluate coherent S-matrix transmittance spectrum from 255-1100nm. Score three objectives: mean transmittance maximization in 255-280nm passband, mean transmittance minimization in 300-700nm visible stopband, mean transmittance minimization in 700-1100nm NIR stopband. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with bound projection. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Applied feedback directive: replaced free-parameter initialization with geometric progression template (r∈[1.08,1.12]) and imposed 85nm HfO2 upper bound to filter absorption-dominated candidates in 255-280nm range.

routes.title: SiO2/HfO2 geometric chirp stack alternative material pair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: SiO2/HfO2 material pair will achieve comparable or better UV transmission than MgF2/HfO2 while maintaining visible/NIR rejection, based on evidence of SiO2/HfO2 long-pass filters with 90%+ transmission from 260nm onward (CorpusId:211025653).
routes.design_principle: Substitute MgF2 with SiO2 as low-index layer while retaining HfO2 high-index layer and geometric chirp principle. SiO2 offers better deposition uniformity and moisture stability per evidence.
routes.proposed_topology: 20-layer alternating stack: air | [SiO2 | HfO2]_10 | fused_silica substrate. Exact layer count: 20 finite layers.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with geometric progression initialization r∈[1.08,1.12]
manufacturing_considerations: SiO2/HfO2 compatible with IAD for moisture stability
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent multilayer interference
SiO2/HfO2 refractive index contrast sufficient for UV bandpass filtering
expected_advantages: SiO2 offers better deposition uniformity than MgF2 per evidence
HfO2/SiO2 stacks demonstrated stable with IAD process
Material pair avoids MgF2 moisture sensitivity issues
known_risks: SiO2 may have higher absorption than MgF2 below 280nm
Lower index contrast may require more layers for same stopband depth

routes.title: Reduced 16-layer geometric chirp MgF2/HfO2 stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer geometric chirp stack will achieve ≥80% of the 20-layer performance while reducing manufacturing complexity and total optical thickness, testing layer-count efficiency tradeoff.
routes.design_principle: Reduce layer count from 20 to 16 while maintaining geometric chirp template (r∈[1.08,1.12]) and 85nm HfO2 cap. Tests whether fewer layers can achieve acceptable performance with simpler fabrication.

routes.title: AR-matched periodic photonic crystal MgF2/HfO2 stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic (L/2 H L/2)m structure with AR matching coatings per CorpusId:199509322 evidence will achieve better passband transmission and stopband rejection than pure chirped stack by leveraging photonic crystal bandgap physics.
routes.design_principle: Implement periodic main-function units (L/2 H L/2)m sandwiched between two anti-reflection coatings as demonstrated in high-performance SiO2/SiNx UV filters. Adapt to MgF2/HfO2 material pair with geometric thickness scaling.
routes.proposed_topology: 22-layer stack: air | AR_coating_3layers | [MgF2/2 | HfO2 | MgF2/2]_8 | AR_coating_3layers | fused_silica substrate. Exact layer count: 22 finite layers (3+16+3).
design_variables: periodic unit thicknesses with geometric progression
theory_basis: AR matching reduces passband reflection losses
Periodic structure provides predictable stopband edges
expected_advantages: AR coatings improve passband transmission per evidence

Demonstrated architecture in CorpusId:199509322 achieved >80% transmission in solar-blind region
known_risks: Periodic structure may have narrower stopband than chirped design
May require precise thickness control for periodicity

routes.revision_reason: Introduced periodic photonic crystal architecture with AR matching based on CorpusId:199509322 evidence, adapting demonstrated SiO2/SiNx design principle to MgF2/HfO2 material pair while retaining geometric chirp initialization from route_02 refinement.
